jobs.name: oc-triage-factory-patrol
jobs.prompt:
Factory-scoped Triage patrol (owner order 2026-09-19: "triage only the internal factory issues").

SCOPE — internal factory issues ONLY: issues about how this dev factory itself works, i.e. fixes landing in tools/** or .github/workflows.
OUT OF SCOPE: src/** (the opencrabs binary) issues, and upstream/harvest lifecycle work (the latter is separately held by the Owner Push Freeze).

SCOPE IS A FILE-SURFACE TEST, NEVER A TITLE-PREFIX TEST (HQ ruling 2026-09-22, v0.4.236 — canon: skills/opencrabs-dev/triage.md §Duty T4). Bucket an issue by the file surface its FIX lands on, read out of the issue BODY, per-issue, BEFORE any dispatch — never by the fix(...) scope in its title. fix(tools): is a LABEL the owner applies to every tool-related issue, and it spans TWO repositories and two buckets: a fix landing in tools/** (skill repo) is IN scope, while a fix landing in src/brain/tools/** or any other src/** path (the daemon binary) is OUT of scope. A title prefix is wrong on BOTH inversions and silent in both — so read the body; where the body names no path, decide the bucket by the fix MECHANISM, not by the prefix.

THE PATH TEST IS A PREFIX TEST, AND THE PATH IS EXISTENCE-TESTED (HQ ruling 2026-09-24, v0.4.246). tools/** means ANY path under tools/ — tools/lib/oc-notify.sh is exactly as in-scope as tools/ship/oc-deploy, so testing only for the tools/oc-* shape buckets a genuine tools/** fix OUT. And a tools/ string in PROSE is not a fix surface: a body that NAMES a path which git ls-files resolves IS the surface. Origin: the 2026-09-24 06:00Z cycle reported #433 as "surface not pinned in the body" and listed it out-of-scope, but #433's body names tools/lib/oc-notify.sh, which EXISTS and is tracked — so it is IN scope, and of that cycle's "three out-of-scope wires" only #419 and #471 actually were.

COHORT ACCOUNTING IS A PREDICATE, NEVER A HAND-LIST (HQ ruling 2026-09-24, v0.4.245). Build the CLAIMED cohort from the canonical predicate (oc_claims.open_claims, tools/lib/oc_claims.py) and the DISPATCHED cohort from the dispatcher's own dedup memory — never by hand and never from recollection. Every in-scope issue must land in EXACTLY ONE bucket, and the BUCKET TOTAL must equal the COVERAGE LIST; print the reconciliation line beside the cohorts. When the two disagree the LIST is wrong, not the buckets.

DO NOT OPEN A PLAN (HQ ruling 2026-09-24, v0.4.246 — origin #510). This session is UNATTENDED: it has no channel binding, so there is NO approval surface. Calling plan init strands the run — the plan sits in Editing with approved_at null forever because no card exists to carry a tap, and because THIS CRON REUSES ITS WORKER SESSION, every later fire re-reads the stranded plan and re-reports a blocker no surface can clear (three consecutive cycles did exactly that). The same applies to init mode=checklist — it ALSO returns to Editing pending approval, so it is not a mitigation. Work the patrol directly and report the result.

Work: sweep open IN-SCOPE fork issues via gh issue list, route unclaimed in-scope issues to domain-affinity editor lanes with a wire envelope, sweep stale contained branches via oc-branch-sweep, and check stalled claims per skills/opencrabs-dev/triage.md (Duty T4 & T5).
